deck: BUY THE LOW-RATE LOAN, NOT THE HOUSE: SUBJECT-TO TAKEOVERS, MIRROR WRAPS, AND SELLER-AS-BANK PITCHES
SELL ON AN EQUITY WRAP FOR SPREAD, DOWN PAYMENT, AND CASH FLOW, THEN SERVICE, DISCLOSE, AND PLAN EVERY NOTE EXIT
site_ui.lead: Practitioners take over existing low-rate loans subject-to, then sell on a wraparound note that earns the spread on the full balance while a third-party servicer pays the underlying lender first.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies on subject-to acquisition, wraparound note arbitrage, seller financing, compliance, servicing, and note exits. Every claim, metric, and quote carries timestamped inline attribution to the practitioner and video it came from.

flow: Pull absentee owners with values above $300,000, at least 20% equity, and two-plus years of ownership, plus preforeclosures that can be bought before auction.

Frame the retail sale as roughly 10% lost to commissions and closing costs, offer to take over payments and cover arrears, and reverse-engineer the seller's monthly number without mentioning interest.

Buy subject-to or on a mirror wrap, assemble the lender access package (SSN, authorization to release, notarized limited POA), and keep the seller's insurance in force with the trust as additional insured.
Open escrow and get the title report before promising a move-out date, then record the deed of trust or mortgage with the wraparound rider as the security instrument, never the note itself.
Sell on an equity wrap that marks up both price and interest rate so the spread runs on the full balance, with disclosure of the existing mortgage and due-on-sale clause up front and at closing.

Route every payment through a servicer that pays the underlying lender first, name a refinance, reserves, and timeline plan if the loan is called, and ask to renew and extend balloons before paying off or selling the note.
